partners.diseaseBName: focal facial dermal dysplasia type IV
partners.mechanism_chain: CYP2R1 (HGNC:25902) —DISRUPTS→ Vitamin D 25-hydroxylation (REACT:R-HSA-720810); Vitamin D 25-hydroxylation (REACT:R-HSA-720810) —DECREASES→ 25-hydroxyvitamin D (CHEBI:26197); 25-hydroxyvitamin D (CHEBI:26197) —LEADS_TO→ Rickets (HP:0005765); CYP26C1 (HGNC:18745) —DISRUPTS→ Retinoid metabolism (REACT:R-HSA-6734035); Retinoid metabolism (REACT:R-HSA-6734035) —LEADS_TO→ Focal facial dermal dysplasia (HP:0030743). Loss-of-function mutations in CYP2R1 impair vitamin D 25-hydroxylation, leading to reduced levels of 25-hydroxyvitamin D and consequently rickets. Concurrently, loss-of-function mutations in CYP26C1 disrupt retinoid metabolism, which has been linked to focal facial dermal dysplasia. The convergence is hypothesized through the shared involvement of these cytochrome P450 enzymes in distinct but potentially interconnected metabolic pathways that influence developmental processes.

falsification.text: Absence of mutations in CYP2R1 in individuals with vitamin D hydroxylation-deficient rickets, type 1B, or absence of mutations in CYP26C1 in individuals with focal facial dermal dysplasia type IV, would falsify this hypothesis. Furthermore, if independent genetic causes for both diseases are definitively established without any shared downstream molecular consequences, this would also serve as falsification.
falsification.gnomad_variant: Identification of common variants (AF > 0.01) in the gnomAD database within the coding regions of CYP2R1 and CYP26C1 that are associated with either disease would challenge the hypothesis of these genes being the sole or primary drivers of these rare conditions.

For instance, if retinoid signaling pathways are indirectly affected by vitamin D deficiency or vice versa, interventions aimed at modulating these pathways could have broader applications. This is particularly relevant for developmental disorders where metabolic dysregulation can have profound effects.

partners.mechanism_chain: CYP2R1 (HGNC:26040) —DISRUPTS→ Vitamin D hydroxylation (GO:0006777); Vitamin D hydroxylation (GO:0006777) —DECREASES→ 25-hydroxyvitamin D (CHEBI:27789); 25-hydroxyvitamin D (CHEBI:27789) —DECREASES→ Vitamin D signaling pathway (WP:2667); VDR (HGNC:12477) —DISRUPTS→ Vitamin D signaling pathway (WP:2667); Vitamin D signaling pathway (WP:2667) —LEADS_TO→ Rickets (HP:0002798); Vitamin D signaling pathway (WP:2667) —LEADS_TO→ Hypophosphatemia (HP:0002137); Vitamin D signaling pathway (WP:2667) —LEADS_TO→ Hypocalcemia (HP:0003128). This knowledge can inform therapeutic strategies, such as the use of calcitriol (the active form of vitamin D) or its analogs in VDR-deficient patients, and potentially different approaches for CYP2R1-deficient patients that bypass the initial hydroxylation step.

partners.mechanism_chain: CYP2R1 (HGNC:24072) —DISRUPTS→ 25-hydroxyvitamin D (CHEBI:63516); 25-hydroxyvitamin D (CHEBI:63516) —DECREASES→ Vitamin D Metabolism (REACT:R-HSA-168763); CYP27B1 (HGNC:24070) —DISRUPTS→ 1,25-dihydroxyvitamin D (CHEBI:17701); 1,25-dihydroxyvitamin D (CHEBI:17701) —DECREASES→ Vitamin D Metabolism (REACT:R-HSA-168763); Vitamin D Metabolism (REACT:R-HSA-168763) —LEADS_TO→ Rickets (HP:0002744); Vitamin D Metabolism (REACT:R-HSA-168763) —LEADS_TO→ Hypocalcemia (HP:0003072); Vitamin D Metabolism (REACT:R-HSA-168763) —LEADS_TO→ Hypophosphatemia (HP:0003075).
